# MapLibre GL

Open-source WebGL vector map renderer, the community fork of Mapbox GL JS from before its licence
change. Used at **5.24.0** in [[farely]] to draw demand zones, the driver's position and venue markers
— with **OpenFreeMap** as the tile source, which needs no key and no account.

## The tiering decision

MapLibre is the single heaviest thing in the bundle: `vite build` splits it into its own **~1 MB
chunk** against a ~309 kB main bundle. Farely responds with two tiers rather than one map:

- **Full tier** — MapLibre is `import()`ed dynamically, so the chunk downloads only when a device is
  judged capable.
- **LITE tier** — `device.ts` sniffs available RAM (2–3 GB thresholds, the "potato phone" tier) and
  substitutes a **hand-rolled DOM/SVG projection**. No WebGL, no 1 MB download, same zones drawn.

That fallback is the sharpest instance in the repo of [[zero-dependency-no-build-step]] surviving at
module level: rather than degrading the feature on weak hardware, the app reimplements the *needed 5 %*
of the library by hand. It is also the right instinct for the actual user — a driver's phone is old,
hot, and already running two navigation apps.

- `TODO:` the 2–3 GB LITE thresholds have no recorded calibration. Whether they were measured against
  a real device the author owns is unknown — not asked at interview.

## The privacy consequence

**Map tiles are an unconditional outbound request.** Every session fetches OpenFreeMap tiles with no
key, no opt-in and no off switch, which is one of the two reasons the README's "runs fully on-device"
claim is overstated — the other being fueleconomy.gov car specs. SRS §4.10 and
`docs/guides/ANDROID-INSTALL.md` list it honestly; the README does not. See
[[on-device-first-inference]] and [[documentation-drift]].

Unlike the [[anthropic-messages-api]] path, no *content* leaves the device here — a tile request leaks
**where the driver is looking**, which is a different and arguably more continuous exposure than one
throttled screen capture. The repo argues carefully about the capture path and never mentions this one.

## What it renders

Demand zones and the venue markers produced by {{event-driven-demand-positioning}}, plus the position
used by the deadhead term in {{deadhead-adjusted-net-profit}} — which is simulated, since no native
location code exists.
